messages.subject: geom_crossbar / colors in legend
parts:
dear list members
 
i've tried to find a solution the whole afternoon. but i had no luck.
my question is similar to this one
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!topic/ggplot2/SKhdVq25tJg
 
example:
 
library (ggplot2)

mean.value <- c(7.2,8.3,6.3,6.2,4.5,5.9)
SE <- c(0.25,0.3,0.4,0.2,0.5,0.6)
names <- c("Test1","Test1","Test2","Test2","Test3","Test3")
gender <- c("Boy","Girl","Boy","Girl","Boy","Girl")
m.data2 <- data.frame (cbind (mean.value,SE),gender,names)

pl  <- ggplot(data=m.data2, aes(x=1,y=mean.value ,min=mean.value-1.96*SE, ymax=mean.value+1.96*SE,fill=gender))
pl  <- pl + geom_crossbar (width=0.8, stat="identity", position="dodge", fatten=2)
pl  <- pl + facet_wrap (~names, nrow=1)
pl  <- pl + scale_y_continuous(name="Result",limits=c(1,10),breaks=(c(1:10)))
pl ### so far, no problem
 
#### i want the same color (fill) in the legend as in the crossbars
#### tried different codes with  stat_smooth () ... but got always an error.
 
pl  <- pl + stat_smooth ()
pl <- pl + scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "blue"))
pl ### not drawing the plot
 
thanks for your help!
 
greg

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: geom_crossbar / colors in legend
parts:
One problem is that it appears you want to apply geom_smooth() across
different panels. That's not going to happen. Assuming that the idea
was to connect the means between tests for each gender, a better way
is to facet by gender, create a numeric version of names, erect error
bar plots and connect the means with lines. The problem with doing the
same using crossbars is that the width of the latter geom gets in the
way. This wasn't meant to be 'ready for publication', but here's the
idea:

# Create a numeric version of names - call it 'test'
m.data2$test <- as.numeric(m.data2$names)

# Error bar plots faceted by gender
ggplot(m.data2, aes(x = test, y = mean.value)) +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean.value - 1.96 * SE,
ymax = mean.value + 1.96 * SE,
colour = names), width = 0.4, size = 1) +
geom_point(aes(colour = names), size = 3) +
geom_line(size = 1) +
scale_y_continuous('Result', limits = c(1, 10), breaks = 1:10) +
scale_x_continuous('Test', limits = c(0, 4), breaks = 1:3) +
scale_colour_manual('test', breaks = levels(m.data2$names),
values = c('blue', 'firebrick', 'orange')) +
facet_wrap(~ gender, nrow = 1)

If you want to see what happens with geom_smooth(), try

last_plot() + geom_smooth()

The result won't be much different from connecting the means in a
piecewise linear fashion and you'll pick up a bunch of warnings.
Moreover, the tests are discrete-valued with no implied ordering, so
geom_smooth() makes no sense in this context. The point of a smoother
is that it fits a function in a continuous 2D region.

Without the line connection, the geom_crossbar() version would look like

# Crossbar plots faceted by gender
ggplot(m.data2, aes(x = test, y = mean.value)) +
geom_crossbar(aes(ymin = mean.value - 1.96 * SE,
ymax = mean.value + 1.96 * SE,
fill = names), width = 0.8) +
scale_y_continuous('Result', limits = c(1, 10), breaks = 1:10) +
scale_x_continuous('Test', limits = c(0, 4), breaks = 1:3) +
scale_fill_manual(breaks = levels(m.data2$names),
values = c('blue', 'firebrick', 'orange')) +
facet_wrap(~ gender, nrow = 1)

Notice that there is no fill color to distinguish among the three
tests - that's the first problem. If you put

last_plot() + geom_line(size = 1)

you'll see that the lines are connected at the center of the boxes,
which IMO is not aesthetically pleasing.

Therefore, I'd suggest the error bar plot with connecting lines if
your intent is to 'connect the means'.

Dennis

in version 0.89 i used geom_smooth just to get a legend with filled
colors!


pl <- pl + geom_smooth (aes(x=0, group = 1), colour="black", alpha=1)

the line above worked in 0.89! crossbars and filled legend had the
same colors.
but it's not working anymore in 0.90. so i tried to adapt the code.
but no luck.
with geom_smooth i want to produce a hidden layer, just to get the
legend i need.

any other ideas to solve my problem?

messages.author: eb97dee87f719076
messages.subject: Re: geom_crossbar / colors in legend
parts:
guys. i found a solution.

legend fill works with geom_crossbar, if i put this additional line of
code

pl <- pl + geom_smooth (aes(x=1,y=0),stat="identity",alpha=1,
color="black")
### stat="identity" was missing
pl

or second solution: additional line:

pl <- pl + geom_bar (aes(x=1,y=mean.value),stat="identity")
### in invisible bar plot
pl

greg
